messages:
Maya T.: Quick design proposal — thinking out loud about a 'seat-assignment ladder' for the roles matrix. Instead of the large role rows + modal invite, we show compact seat types inline (Full, Power, Read-only, Guest) with a small ladder UI to assign levels. Goal: make bulk assignments faster and reduce clicks in the invite flow. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/seat-ladder-proto :eyes:

Aran K.: I like the idea for power users. two quick concerns: 1) keyboard focus order on the ladder — needs to be linear and announced, 2) how does this map to seat billing? we need a clear affordance that Guest seats are free vs Full seat count.

Maya T.: yea good call. proposal: ladder items are tabbable, each has `aria-pressed` state and an accessible name like "Assign Full seat — includes edit+deploy". For billing hint, small tag `Billed` or `Free` next to seat label.

Lucas P.: Copy nit: instead of "Assign" maybe use "Set role" on the ladder control. "Invite" should remain for emailing external people. So two flows: "Set role" (in-org quick assign) vs "Invite" (send email). Could we put a small tooltip that clarifies? e.g., tooltip text: "Set role for existing members — does not send invite email."

Samira R.: Accessibility nits: ensure contrast on the ladder active state (need 4.5:1); provide `aria-describedby` linking to the billing hint; for the tooltip use `role=tooltip` and ensure it appears on focus. Also ensure the compact ladder isn't the only way to access role details — screen reader users should be able to open a detail panel.

Maya T.: thanks — I'll add the aria-describedby. thinking about audit logs: when seat changes happen via ladder, we should emit a structured audit entry like "seat.change: {actor, from, to, method: 'ladder'}" so SRE and security can filter easily. DesignBot, can we show how that looks in the audit navigation?

DesignBot: mock audit entry in dev console:
```
{
  "event": "seat.change",
  "actor": "maya.t@redwood.com",
  "target": "jordan@example.com",
  "from": "Guest",
  "to": "Power",
  "method": "ladder",
  "timestamp": "2025-03-12T16:24:12Z"
}
```
Use that to link from the role row to the audit panel (right-hand rail). :white_check_mark:

Aran K.: Small UX ask: if a customer has mixed SSO settings, the ladder should show an SSO lock icon for seats that are SSO-enforced (can't downgrade). Hover state: explain "SSO enforced by org policy". For keyboard users, the locked seat should be `aria-disabled` with an explanation in the adjacent description.

Lucas P.: We should also add a quick undo toast after changes: "Changed Jordan from Guest → Power — undo" (aria-live polite). That helps reduce accidental assignments. Copy for the toast should be short — good example: `Changed Jordan to Power — Undo`

Samira R.: On contrast again — the undo button in the toast needs a visible focus ring. Also test with high-contrast OS mode. For screen readers, use `role=status` so the change is announced but doesn't steal focus.

Maya T.: Implementation checklist I'm going to hand to eng: 
- ladder component with keyboard linear navigation
- ARIA: `aria-pressed`, `aria-describedby` to billing/note, `aria-disabled` for SSO locks
- copy: use "Set role" for in-org, keep "Invite" for external; toast text as above
- audit: emit structured `seat.change` events for the audit log link
- visuals: meet 4.5:1 contrast on active and hover states; visible focus rings

Maya T.: tagging for follow-ups: @Aran K. can you put the keyboard nav spec? @Samira R. can you run the accessibility checklist once prototype is updated? @Lucas P. please review the copy strings in context. I'll update the Figma and ping dev when ready. :sparkles:

Aran K.: will do — I'll add the focus map tonight. :white_check_mark:

Samira R.: happy to run the a11y pass once it's in Figma, prefer to test with VoiceOver and NVDA.

Lucas P.: I'll tweak microcopy and push a small doc with string variants. :memo:

DesignBot: File updated: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/seat-ladder-proto?node-id=12:34 — note: ladder component ID `comp_ldr_9`

Maya T.: great — thanks team. landing this in next design review on Friday. :rocket:
